metadata.title: Bangladesh HSC Science: Physics and Chemistry Constants Reference
metadata.target: Bangladesh HSC Science curriculum; Physics 1st and 2nd Papers, Chemistry 1st and 2nd Papers
metadata.scope: A syllabus-mapped, high-coverage reference of fundamental constants, conventional HSC approximations, condition-dependent reference values, unit conversions, important mathematical constants and common school atomic masses.
important_limitations: No individual NCTB textbook edition or publisher text was supplied; the chapter map was checked against publicly available Bangladesh HSC chapter indexes and a recent HSC 2027 school syllabus distribution, and numerical constants were cross-checked against NIST/CODATA and other institutional references.

The file distinguishes universal/defined constants from approximations and material-/condition-dependent reference values. Not every tabulated quantity in every publisher's textbook is a universal constant.

Some advanced supplementary constants are included because they are relevant to named HSC topics, but they may not need to be memorized for the Bangladesh board examination unless specified in the text/question.
Use the value and unit explicitly supplied by an exam question when it conflicts with a rounded reference value here; textbook questions commonly use rounded values for arithmetic simplicity.
metadata.value_precision_policy: Modern fixed/fundamental values generally use CODATA 2022 (NIST page indicates data content updated May 2024). HSC-friendly approximations are separate fields. Condition-dependent values state the conditions where known.

unit_systems_guide.SI: International System of Units; preferred for most HSC calculations.
unit_systems_guide.CGS: centimetre–gram–second; energy is often in erg, mass in g and length in cm.
unit_systems_guide.chemistry_customary: Common litre–atmosphere, bar, torr, calorie and molar units used in chemistry calculations.
unit_systems_guide.mixed: Consistent combinations such as eV, L·kPa or MeV/c²; dimensions must be checked.
unit_systems_guide.dimensionless: No physical unit. Relative atomic mass, refractive index and mathematical constants are dimensionless.

symbol_notes: The letter e can mean elementary charge or Euler's number; they are separate entries here.
The symbol R may mean molar gas constant, Rydberg constant, radius or resistance depending on context; use the chapter/formula context.
The symbol k may mean Coulomb's constant, Boltzmann's constant, spring constant or another quantity; the full label disambiguates it.
The Greek letter σ is used for the Stefan–Boltzmann constant and also for other quantities such as surface charge density; interpret by formula.

constants.name: Speed of light in vacuum
constants.definition_or_meaning: Speed of electromagnetic radiation in vacuum.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Electromagnetic Induction and AC; Optics; Modern Physics; Astronomy
notes: Exact by SI definition.

constants.name: Newtonian constant of gravitation
constants.definition_or_meaning: Proportionality constant in Newton's law of gravitation.
notes: Measured; the parenthetical digits in the CODATA value indicate standard uncertainty.

constants.name: Standard acceleration of gravity
constants.definition_or_meaning: Conventional reference acceleration, not the local acceleration at every location.
constants.common_hsc_approximation: 9.8 m/s² or 10 m/s² when explicitly allowed
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Newtonian Mechanics; Gravitation and Gravity
notes: Do not confuse g₀ with local gravitational acceleration g.

constants.name: Earth-surface gravitational acceleration (approximate)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Representative value near Earth's surface; varies with latitude, altitude, geology and convention.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Newtonian Mechanics; Gravitation and Gravity
notes: This is not a universal constant. Use the value stated by the question when provided.

constants.name: Planck constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Relates photon energy to frequency: E = hν.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Physical Optics; Introduction to Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Exact by SI definition.

constants.name: Reduced Planck constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Planck constant divided by 2π.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Commonly written h-bar; exact underlying value follows h and the mathematical value of π.

constants.name: Elementary charge magnitude
constants.definition_or_meaning: Magnitude of the charge of a proton; an electron carries charge -e.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Static Electricity; Current Electricity; Modern Physics; Nuclear Physics; Semiconductor and Electronics
notes: For electrons, the signed charge is −e. CGS electrostatic charge units are system-dependent; use SI in most HSC calculations.

constants.name: Avogadro constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Number of specified elementary entities per mole.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases
Chemistry 1st: Chemical Changes; Chemistry 2nd: Environmental Chemistry; Quantitative Chemistry
notes: Exact by SI definition. 'Avogadro's number' is the numerical value; the constant has unit mol^-1.

constants.name: Boltzmann constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Relates average microscopic energy scale to absolute temperature.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases
Chemistry 1st: Chemical Changes; Chemistry 2nd: Environmental Chemistry; Quantitative Chemistry
notes: Exact by SI definition.

constants.name: Molar (universal) gas constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Constant in the ideal-gas equation PV=nRT.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases
Chemistry 1st: Chemical Changes; Chemistry 2nd: Environmental Chemistry; Quantitative Chemistry
notes: Choose the version whose pressure and volume units match the problem. 1 cal_th = 4.184 J; textbook rounded values differ slightly.

constants.name: Faraday constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Electric charge carried by one mole of elementary charges.
notes: For school calculations, 96500 C mol^-1 is common. The sign of charge is handled separately in reaction stoichiometry.

constants.name: Unified atomic mass constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: One twelfth of the mass of a neutral carbon-12 atom in its ground state.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
Chemistry 1st: Periodic Properties; Chemistry 2nd: Quantitative Chemistry
notes: The numerical value 1 g mol^-1 is closely related to the molar mass constant; do not confuse u (mass of one particle) with g mol^-1 (molar mass).

constants.name: Electron rest mass
constants.definition_or_meaning: Rest mass of the electron.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics; Semiconductor and Electronics
notes: Use the precision required by the question.

constants.name: Proton rest mass
constants.definition_or_meaning: Rest mass of the proton.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: A proton is slightly less massive than a neutral hydrogen atom and is not exactly 1 u.

constants.name: Neutron rest mass
constants.definition_or_meaning: Rest mass of the neutron.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: For nuclear mass-defect calculations, follow the mass convention specified in the problem (atomic masses versus bare nuclear/particle masses).

constants.name: Vacuum electric permittivity
constants.definition_or_meaning: Constant appearing in SI electrostatics and Maxwell equations.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Static Electricity; Electromagnetic Induction and AC
notes: Since the 2019 SI redefinition, μ₀ is measured and ε₀ is related to μ₀ and c; the older school approximation μ₀ = 4π × 10^-7 is rounded rather than exact.

constants.name: Vacuum magnetic permeability
constants.definition_or_meaning: Magnetic constant in SI electromagnetism.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism; Electromagnetic Induction and AC
notes: 4π × 10^-7 H/m was exact in the pre-2019 SI system; use it as a school approximation, not the current exact definition.

constants.name: Coulomb constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Proportionality factor in Coulomb's law in SI vacuum.

values.formatted: numerical factor 1 in the Gaussian-cgs Coulomb law

notes: The CGS note refers to the Gaussian electrostatic convention; it is not a direct unit conversion of the SI numerical value.

constants.name: Fine-structure constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Dimensionless electromagnetic coupling constant.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Usually unnecessary for routine HSC calculations unless specifically introduced.

constants.name: Rydberg constant (infinite nuclear mass limit)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Wavenumber constant in hydrogen-like spectral formula for an infinitely massive nucleus.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: For actual hydrogen, the finite proton mass gives a slightly different hydrogen-specific Rydberg constant R_H.

constants.name: Hydrogen spectral Rydberg constant (approx.)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Rydberg wavenumber constant for ordinary hydrogen, accounting for the proton's finite mass.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: For HSC, the question/book may use 1.097 × 10^7 m^-1 without distinguishing R_H and R∞.

constants.name: Bohr radius
constants.definition_or_meaning: Characteristic radius of the ground-state Bohr hydrogen orbit.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: This is a characteristic quantum length, not a literal classical path in modern quantum mechanics.

constants.name: Rydberg energy / hydrogen ground-state ionization-energy scale
constants.definition_or_meaning: Magnitude of the hydrogenic ground-state binding-energy scale.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: The ground-state energy of hydrogen is approximately −13.6 eV; the binding/ionization energy is stated as positive 13.6 eV.

constants.name: Electron rest energy
constants.definition_or_meaning: Energy equivalent of the electron rest mass.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Introduction to Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Use E=mc²; the MeV form is convenient in particle/nuclear calculations.

constants.name: Proton rest energy
constants.definition_or_meaning: Energy equivalent of proton rest mass.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Introduction to Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Often rounded to 938 MeV/c² for proton mass.

constants.name: Neutron rest energy
constants.definition_or_meaning: Energy equivalent of neutron rest mass.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Approximate values are adequate unless the problem gives more precision.

constants.name: Electronvolt
constants.definition_or_meaning: Energy acquired by a particle of elementary charge magnitude moving through a potential difference of one volt.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: eV is a unit of energy, not a separate fundamental constant. It is included because it is used as a fixed conversion value.

constants.name: Stefan–Boltzmann constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Coefficient in ideal blackbody radiant exitance M = σT⁴.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Thermodynamics (if thermal radiation is included); Astronomy
notes: The symbol σ is also used for surface charge density or other quantities in some contexts; interpret by formula.

constants.name: Wien displacement constant
constants.definition_or_meaning: Constant in the blackbody wavelength-displacement relation λ_max T = b.
notes: This is distinct from Wien's frequency-displacement constant.

constants.name: Standard-state pressure (IUPAC convention)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Common reference pressure for thermodynamic standard states.
constants.common_hsc_approximation: Use 1 bar when a chemistry question explicitly means standard state; many school gas problems instead use 1 atm
notes: Standard pressure of 1 bar is not the same as standard atmosphere (1 atm = 101.325 kPa). Always use the problem's stated convention.

constants.name: Standard atmosphere
constants.definition_or_meaning: Conventional pressure unit equal to exactly 101,325 Pa.
notes: Use atm only with the compatible version of R or convert pressure to SI.

constants.name: Common gas-law reference temperature
constants.definition_or_meaning: 0 °C expressed on the thermodynamic temperature scale.
constants.common_hsc_approximation: 273 K or 273.15 K depending on required precision
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases
notes: This is a reference temperature, not a thermodynamic law. Not every use of the term NTP/STP uses the same pressure/temperature convention.

constants.name: Ideal-gas molar volume at 273.15 K and 100 kPa
constants.definition_or_meaning: Ideal-gas molar volume at 0 °C and IUPAC standard-state pressure 100 kPa.
constants.common_hsc_approximation: about 22.71 L mol^-1 at 0 °C and 100 kPa
notes: This differs from 22.414 L/mol because the pressure convention differs.

constants.name: Ideal-gas molar volume at 273.15 K and 1 atm
constants.definition_or_meaning: Ideal-gas molar volume at 0 °C and standard atmospheric pressure 101.325 kPa.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases
notes: The classic school value 22.4 L/mol assumes 273.15 K and 1 atm. Clearly label the convention when reporting it.

constants.name: Loschmidt number density at 273.15 K and 100 kPa
constants.definition_or_meaning: Number of ideal-gas particles per unit volume at specified reference conditions.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases
notes: Condition-specific, not a universal fixed number density.

constants.name: Loschmidt number density at 273.15 K and 1 atm
constants.definition_or_meaning: Number density for an ideal gas at 0 °C and 1 atm.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases
notes: Condition-specific and therefore different from the 100 kPa value.

constants.name: Density of liquid water (reference approximation)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Convenient approximate liquid-water density near its maximum-density temperature.
formula_uses: Physics 1st: Structural Properties of Matter; dimensional/unit problems
notes: Density varies with temperature, pressure and purity; it is not a universal constant.

constants.name: Specific heat capacity of liquid water (reference approximation)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Heat capacity per unit mass per unit temperature rise, near ordinary temperatures.
notes: The value changes slightly with temperature. Many HSC questions use 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1 or provide a value.

constants.name: Specific latent heat of fusion of ice (approximate)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Energy required to melt unit mass of ice at its melting point at ordinary pressure.
notes: A reference property, not universal; depends on pressure and material.

constants.name: Specific latent heat of vaporization of water (approximate)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Energy required to vaporize unit mass of water at its boiling point at ordinary pressure.
notes: Strongly condition-dependent; lower at other temperatures and tends to zero at the critical point.

constants.name: Earth mass (astronomical reference)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Reference mass of Earth, useful in gravity/orbit estimates.
notes: The product GM is known more precisely than separate masses in some celestial calculations; school work usually rounds this value.

constants.name: Earth mean radius (astronomical reference)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Representative mean radius of Earth.
notes: Earth is not a perfect sphere; radius depends on whether equatorial, polar or mean radius is intended.

constants.name: Moon-surface gravitational acceleration (approximate)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Representative gravitational acceleration near the Moon's surface.
notes: Not a universal constant; local value varies slightly with lunar location.

constants.name: Earth escape speed near surface (approximate)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Idealized escape speed from the surface of Earth, ignoring atmosphere and rotation.
notes: Derived from v_esc = sqrt(2GM/R); not a separate fundamental constant.

constants.name: Astronomical unit
constants.definition_or_meaning: IAU-defined unit of length approximately equal to the mean Earth–Sun distance.
notes: IAU symbol is lower-case au; AU is common in school materials.

constants.name: Light-year
constants.definition_or_meaning: Distance traveled by light in vacuum in one Julian year (365.25 days).
notes: An astronomical distance unit; it is not a unit of time.

constants.name: Parsec
constants.definition_or_meaning: Distance at which one astronomical unit subtends one arcsecond.
notes: Use pc for parsec; kpc = 10^3 pc and Mpc = 10^6 pc.

constants.name: Solar mass (astronomical reference)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Representative mass of the Sun.
notes: Rounded conventional reference; not an exact defining constant for the Sun's evolving physical mass.

constants.name: Solar radius (astronomical reference)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Representative photospheric radius of the Sun.
notes: Conventional reference radius; details depend on definition of the solar surface.

constants.name: Solar luminosity (astronomical reference)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Representative total radiant power of the Sun.
notes: The Sun varies slightly; this is a conventional nominal reference.

constants.name: Total solar irradiance near Earth's orbit (approximate)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Solar power received per unit area near 1 au before atmospheric absorption.
notes: Varies with solar activity and orbital distance; include only if used in the astronomy chapter or a question.

constants.name: Empirical nuclear-radius coefficient
constants.definition_or_meaning: Coefficient in nuclear-radius scaling R ≈ r₀ A^(1/3).
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Empirical model coefficient, not an exact universal constant; different textbooks may use approximately 1.1–1.3 fm.

constants.name: Nuclear magneton
constants.definition_or_meaning: Natural unit of magnetic moment for nuclear particles.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Usually beyond routine HSC numerical needs; included as a related atomic/nuclear reference.

constants.name: Bohr magneton
constants.definition_or_meaning: Natural unit of magnetic moment associated with the electron.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics
notes: Supplementary atomic constant; may not be required by the core HSC textbook.

constants.name: Electron charge-to-mass ratio magnitude
constants.definition_or_meaning: Magnitude of electron charge divided by electron rest mass.
formula_uses: Physics 2nd: Magnetic Effects; Introduction to Modern Physics
notes: Some older physics problems use experimental e/m results; this is the modern reference value.

constants.name: Ion product of water at 25 °C
constants.definition_or_meaning: Equilibrium constant for water autoionization under the common dilute-solution convention.

values.formatted: approximately 1.0 × 10^-14 when expressed with standard-state activities

notes: Not temperature-independent. More rigorous thermodynamic equilibrium constants are defined through activities and are dimensionless; HSC concentration-based problems usually use the simplified concentration form.

constants.name: Standard hydrogen electrode potential (conventional zero)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Reference electrode potential assigned zero by convention at standard conditions.
notes: This does not mean every electrode potential is zero; standard potentials are defined relative to this reference and depend on the redox couple.

constants.name: RT/F at 25 °C
constants.definition_or_meaning: Thermal voltage factor in the Nernst equation at T = 298.15 K.
notes: Changes linearly with absolute temperature T.

constants.name: 2.303RT/F at 25 °C
constants.definition_or_meaning: Base-10 logarithmic Nernst-equation factor at T = 298.15 K.
notes: For an n-electron cell, the common term is (0.05916/n) log₁₀Q at 25 °C; the sign and quotient orientation depend on the form of the Nernst equation used.

constants.name: Refractive index of vacuum
constants.definition_or_meaning: Ratio c/v for light in a vacuum; vacuum is the reference medium.
notes: In a material n = c/v and depends on wavelength, temperature, and material conditions.

constants.name: Speed of sound in dry air near 20 °C (illustrative)
constants.definition_or_meaning: Approximate sound speed in dry air near room temperature.
notes: Depends on temperature, humidity, composition and gas properties; do not treat it as a universal constant.

mathematical_constants_used_in_physics_a.name: Euler's number (not elementary charge)
relevance: radioactive decay and differential equations, where used

mathematical_constants_used_in_physics_a.name: Natural logarithm of 10
relevance: converting between natural and base-10 logarithms; pH and Nernst equation contexts

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Heat-capacity ratio for a monatomic ideal gas
condition_dependent_reference_values.conditions: Ideal-gas model with only translational degrees of freedom active.
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Model-based reference, not true for all gases under all conditions.
chapters: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Heat-capacity ratio for a diatomic ideal gas at ordinary temperature
condition_dependent_reference_values.conditions: Ideal diatomic gas with rotational modes active and vibrational modes approximately inactive.
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: A useful model approximation; actual gases and temperatures can differ.
chapters: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Density of dry air near 15 °C and 1 atm
condition_dependent_reference_values.conditions: Approximately dry air at 15 °C and standard atmospheric pressure.
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Strongly depends on temperature, pressure and humidity.
chapters: Physics 1st: Structural Properties of Matter; Dynamics

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Refractive index of air in visible light
condition_dependent_reference_values.conditions: Approximate ordinary air near standard atmospheric conditions and visible wavelengths.
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Depends on pressure, temperature, humidity and wavelength.

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Refractive index of liquid water in visible light
condition_dependent_reference_values.conditions: Approximate visible-light value near room temperature.
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Depends on wavelength, temperature and water purity.

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Refractive index of ordinary glass (illustrative)
condition_dependent_reference_values.conditions: Typical approximate value for some common optical glasses in visible light.
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Not a single glass constant: actual glass composition and wavelength matter. Use the problem's value.

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Electrical resistivity of copper near 20 °C
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Varies with purity, temperature and material condition.

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Electrical resistivity of aluminium near 20 °C
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Varies with alloy, purity and temperature.

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Electrical resistivity of nichrome (illustrative)
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Different nichrome formulations have different resistivity; use supplied values when available.

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Absolute zero temperature
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: A temperature reference, not a material property. The Celsius/Fahrenheit values are conventional exact-scale conversions.

condition_dependent_reference_values.name: Room-temperature convention often used in chemistry
condition_dependent_reference_values.conditions: 25 °C convention often used for pH and standard electrochemistry tables.
condition_dependent_reference_values.notes: Room temperature is not universally fixed; this is a common reference convention.

derived_formula_reference.description: Use R for amount in moles; use k_B for number N of particles.
chapters: Physics 1st: Ideal Gas and Kinetic Theory of Gases

derived_formula_reference.description: Charge transferred by one mole of elementary charges; use charge number/electron stoichiometry separately.

derived_formula_reference.description: For photon energy; convert eV and J consistently.
Use particle rest masses or atomic masses according to the problem's convention.
chapters: Physics 2nd: Modern Physics; Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics

derived_formula_reference.description: Ideal Bohr-model hydrogen energy levels; more accurate values include corrections beyond basic HSC level.
chapters: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics

derived_formula_reference.description: Empirical nuclear radius relation; coefficient varies slightly by textbook/model.
chapters: Physics 2nd: Atomic Model and Nuclear Physics

derived_formula_reference.description: λ is the nuclide-specific decay constant; ln(2) is a mathematical constant.

formula_notes: For a reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, Kc = [C]^c[D]^d/([A]^a[B]^b), with the exact expression following equilibrium conventions.

For gas equilibria, Kp is related to Kc through Kp = Kc(RT)^(Δn_g) when compatible pressure/concentration conventions are used; in rigorous thermodynamics equilibrium constants are dimensionless activities.
